gaza|2026-11-05|deir el balah az zawayda.place: Deir el-Balah / az-Zawayda / Bureij / Khan Younis
gaza|2026-11-05|deir el balah az zawayda.text: 5 Nov — Deir el-Balah / az-Zawayda / Bureij / Khan Younis: Israeli drone strikes and gunfire killed at least four people, including a man in a displacement tent and a child in Bureij, according to medical sources; the Health Ministry's post-ceasefire toll reached 1,602 killed.

gaza|2026-11-06|khan younis|armed-attack.text: 6 Nov — Khan Younis: A teenager was killed by Israeli fire; other reports put the day's toll across Gaza at five, including a 12-year-old boy and a woman.

gaza|2026-11-10|gaza city|airstrike.text: 10 Nov — Gaza City: Two Israeli air strikes killed three people, including a child, according to Palestinian medical authorities cited by Reuters.

gaza|2026-11-10|khan younis|armed-attack.text: 10 Nov — Khan Younis (coast and town): Israeli forces shot two people, killing one, and the Israeli navy fired on fishing boats, wounding a fisherman and damaging two boats.

lebanon|2026-11-04|qabrikha|drone-strike.text: 4 Nov — Qabrikha (Marjayoun district): An Israeli drone strike on a motorcycle killed one person and wounded another, according to the Health Ministry. Israel said it targeted Hezbollah members; residents said both were Amal-affiliated rescue workers. The ministry's toll since 2 March stands at 4,390 killed.

lebanon|2026-11-06|bint jbeil|airstrike.text: 6 Nov — Bint Jbeil: Israeli air strike reported by Lebanese state media; no casualty figures were given.

lebanon|2026-11-07|bani hayyan zawtar al.text: 7 Nov — Bani Hayyan / Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh: Israeli forces carried out a detonation in Bani Hayyan and shelled Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh, according to Lebanese media.

lebanon|2026-11-10|qantara al mansouri m.text: 10 Nov — Qantara / al-Mansouri / Majdal Zoun: An Israeli air strike hit Qantara, and artillery fire hit around al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun, according to Lebanese state media.

iran|2026-11-06|qeshm island|missile-str.text: 6 Nov — Qeshm Island: US strikes hit the island with two projectiles, part of a weeks-long series against Iranian air defences and launchers; Trump called them 'minor strikes'. Iranian state media reported further US projectiles and explosions on Qeshm on 8 Nov.

iran|ongoing|strait of hormuz|maritime.text: 1–6 Nov — Strait of Hormuz: UKMTO recorded at least 11 ships attacked in and around the strait, three of which sank. The IRGC and Iran's army claimed to have downed a US MQ-1 (6 Nov) and an MQ-9 (7 Nov).

iran|2026-11-07|off khasab musandam|mari.text: 7 Nov — Off Khasab (Musandam): A tanker caught fire and its crew evacuated, and UKMTO later reclassified the incident as an attack; Iran's navy claimed a tanker running without a transponder hit a mine.

iran|2026-11-10|off limah oman uae water.text: 10 Nov — Off Limah (Oman) / UAE waters: UKMTO said a tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile 19 nm north-east of Limah (crew safe), and ADNOC said one of its vessels was damaged in an attack in UAE territorial waters; the IRGC claimed two tankers caught fire using an unauthorised route.

yemen|2026-11-06|al hadara market al waz.text: 6 Nov — al-Hadara market, al-Waziyah (Taiz province): A strike on a vegetable market killed at least 20–30 people according to Houthi officials (22 killed and 30 injured in another count). The Houthis blamed Saudi F-15s; the government blamed a Houthi ballistic missile, and AP could not verify either account.

yemen|2026-11-06|taiz fronts|ground-clas.text: 6 Nov — Taiz fronts: Government forces claimed to have retaken al-Nidani, Shaab al-Sarari, parts of Sanamat and Ribat al-Qarn; OCHA reports more than 323,000 people displaced since August, and about 800,000 people in Taiz are cut off from supplies.

yemen|2026-11-08|saada sanaa|airstrike.text: 8 Nov — Saada / Sanaa: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in Saada and one in Sanaa used against Riyadh and the Eastern Province.

yemen|2026-11-10|sanaa hodeidah saada|ai.text: 10 Nov — Sanaa / Hodeidah / Saada: Coalition air strikes hit the state oil company in Sanaa, wounding six according to Houthi-affiliated media, with further strikes on Hodeidah and Saada; on 9 Nov government forces reported advances in Lahj.

israel|2026-11-08|jerusalem|political.text: 8 Nov — Jerusalem: President Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government after 67 MKs recommended him against 46 for Netanyahu; he has 28 days, extendable by 14.

israel|2026-11-06|duma burin west bank|u.text: 6 Nov — Duma / Burin (south of Nablus, West Bank): Settlers burned tents in Duma and cut power lines in Burin.

israel|2026-11-10|burqa west bank|armed-.text: 10 Nov — Burqa (near Nablus, West Bank): Israeli forces killed 14-year-old Moataz Iyad Daghlas during a raid and wounded two other young men; the army said soldiers fired to stop stone-throwing at vehicles.

israel|2026-11-10|near nablus west bank|.text: 10 Nov — Near Nablus (West Bank): Settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives, injuring a photojournalist.

iraq|2026-11-04|balisan valley north eas.text: 4 Nov — Balisan valley (north-east of Erbil) / Halabja: Iranian drones struck a Komala headquarters and a house in Halabja province, causing property damage; no casualties were reported at Halabja.

iraq|2026-11-05|kirkuk|military-activity.text: 5 Nov — Kirkuk: The Counter-Terrorism Service detained an Islamic State suspect amid concern over ISIS sleeper cells in Kirkuk and Garmian.

iraq|2026-11-06|kirkuk|other.text: 6 Nov — Kirkuk: The National Security Service found an explosive-laden drone and destroyed it in a controlled detonation; its origin was not established.

iraq|2026-11-05|baghdad|diplomatic.text: 5 Nov — Baghdad: Trump spoke with Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi about regional security, and US envoy Tom Barrack visited Baghdad.

saudi arabia|2026-11-08|riyadh eastern p.text: 8 Nov — Riyadh / Eastern Province: The coalition said air defences intercepted ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and the Eastern Province (counts vary from three to five missiles plus a drone), after loud explosions were heard in the capital.

saudi arabia|2026-11-08|riyadh financial.text: 8 Nov — Riyadh (financial district): The Ministry of Energy said an Aramco administrative building was hit in an attempted attack, causing minor damage and no casualties; the Houthis claimed hits on King Khalid airport, Aramco storage and Abqaiq.

saudi arabia|2026-11-10|riyadh abqaiq|mi.text: 10 Nov — Riyadh / Abqaiq: Saudi forces intercepted two Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh; the Houthis claimed strikes on King Khalid airport, the financial district, pipeline pumping stations and Aramco infrastructure at Abqaiq (unverified).

saudi arabia|2026-11-08|riyadh|military-.text: 8 Nov — Riyadh: A Syrian official told AP that about 600 Syrian special forces will deploy to Saudi Arabia within a week, following the 5 Nov Saudi–Syrian defence cooperation agreement.

syria|ongoing|quneitra western daraa|mil.text: 1–5 Nov — Quneitra / western Daraa: The Sijil Center recorded at least 66 Israeli violations, including incursions, checkpoints, home raids, detentions of olive pickers in Wadi Kuya, and artillery shells near al-Mantara Dam; no casualties were reported.

syria|2026-11-06|al samdaniyah al sharqi.text: 6 Nov — al-Samdaniyah al-Sharqiyah (Quneitra countryside): Israeli forces fired artillery at the village, according to Syrian state media.

syria|2026-11-05|aleppo|military-activit.text: 5 Nov — Aleppo: Authorities dismantled an ISIS cell they said was linked to a series of attacks and assassinations in the province.

syria|2026-11-08|damascus|military-activ.text: 8 Nov — Damascus: Syria confirmed it will send about 600 special forces to Saudi Arabia to support the fight against the Houthis, after al-Sharaa and MBS signed a defence cooperation agreement on 5 Nov.

egypt|2026-11-08|tripoli libya|diplomati.text: 8 Nov — Tripoli (Libya): Egypt reopened its embassy in Tripoli after a 12-year closure, with Foreign Minister Abdelatty attending.

jordan|2026-11-05|amman near the sri lan.text: 5 Nov — Amman (near the Sri Lankan embassy): A stabbing attack on a security post killed one officer and wounded another. The suspect, an ISIS-linked convict recently released after a 2020 terrorism case, was arrested; authorities called it a planned 'terrorist attack'.

jordan|2026-11-05|karak irbid marka zarq.text: 5–6 Nov — Karak / Irbid / Marka / Zarqa: Security agencies carried out sweeping overnight raids across several governorates after the Amman attack.

jordan|2026-11-03|amman|political.text: 3 Nov — Amman: Prosecutors charged three suspects in the 23 Oct Karak church attack (nine killed, about 40 wounded) with terrorism offences carrying the death penalty and referred the case to the State Security Court.

jordan|2026-11-09|eastern border|other.text: 9 Nov — Eastern border: The Eastern Military Zone foiled an attempt to smuggle a large quantity of narcotics using guided balloons.

libya|2026-11-04|eastern libya|diplomati.text: 4 Nov — Eastern Libya: Niger signed a memorandum of understanding with Khalifa Haftar's command to expand bilateral cooperation.

libya|2026-11-08|tripoli|diplomatic.text: 8 Nov — Tripoli: Egypt reopened its embassy after a 12-year closure on security grounds.

libya|2026-11-08|tripoli|political.text: 8 Nov — Tripoli: PM Dbeibah met UN envoy Hanna Tetteh to review the UN-sponsored 4+4 committee's work on the electoral commission and election timetable; no armed clashes were found in reporting for 5–12 Nov.

tunisia|2026-10-23|tunis jebiniana|unres.text: 23 Oct — Tunis / Jebiniana (Sfax governorate): Rare unrest broke out over recent deaths linked to the police; protesters burned a vehicle and tyres, and police fired tear gas.

tunisia|2026-10-17|tunis|unrest.text: 17 Oct — Tunis: Thousands joined the largest protest against President Saied in years, over economic hardship and restrictions on political freedoms, with hundreds of police deployed.

ukraine|2026-11-06|komyshuvakha zaporizh.text: 6 Nov — Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia Oblast): The death toll from the 2 November guided-bomb strike on an aid-distribution school and shelter rose to at least 50 after more bodies were recovered, and CNN cites local authorities confirming 53, making it Russia's deadliest strike of 2026. On 8 November a drone again targeted emergency workers at the site, per the State Emergency Service.

ukraine|2026-11-09|odesa|drone-strike.text: 9 Nov — Odesa: A Russian attack killed three people and seriously wounded one, per the city military administration. Russia also struck three power substations and a cargo ship in the Black Sea that Moscow claimed was carrying arms; Ukraine's Energy Ministry counted 128 attacks on the energy sector in the past week.

ukraine|2026-11-11|nationwide|missile-st.text: 10–11 Nov — Nationwide: An overnight attack with 163 drones (91 jet-powered), a Kh-59/69 and Banderol/Dan-T cruise missiles killed 9 and injured 39 over the day, including 3 dead in Dnipropetrovsk, 2 in Donetsk, 2 in Odesa, 1 in Kherson and 1 in Zaporizhzhia oblasts. Power outages were reported in eight oblasts including Kyiv, Kharkiv and Odesa.

ukraine|2026-11-11|abu dhabi uae|diploma.text: 10–11 Nov — Abu Dhabi (UAE): US-mediated trilateral talks with Russia ended with agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange, expected within two to three weeks, but no ceasefire or territorial agreement. Arakhamia cited 'good momentum' and called for Europe to join future rounds.

russia|2026-11-09|kirishi leningrad obla.text: 9 Nov — Kirishi (Leningrad Oblast): Ukrainian drones set the KINEF refinery, Russia's second-largest, on fire, hitting at least one crude-processing unit. Governor Drozdenko said 113 drones were downed; Al Jazeera reported him saying a woman was killed by debris, while Kyiv Post reported no injuries in Kirishi. Ukraine's General Staff also claimed a strike on the Rostec-owned Morozov plant, which makes explosives and Iskander propellant.

russia|2026-11-08|kursk oblast|drone-str.text: 8 Nov — Kursk Oblast: One person was killed when a Ukrainian drone hit a tractor, per Governor Khinshtein (Reuters).

russia|2026-11-12|graivoron district bel.text: 11–12 Nov — Graivoron district (Belgorod Oblast): One civilian was killed and eight injured over the past day, per the regional governor. Russia's Defence Ministry claimed 71 Ukrainian drones downed overnight into 12 November over seven regions and Crimea.

russia|2026-11-12|moscow|diplomatic.text: 12 Nov — Moscow: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrived to brief Putin on the Abu Dhabi talks, which ended on 11 November with a prisoner-exchange agreement but no ceasefire; Medinsky said Moscow is not opposed to EU participation in future talks.

belarus|2026-11-03|minsk|political.text: 3 Nov — Minsk: At the Minsk International Conference on Eurasian Security, Lukashenka warned that cost-of-living protests across Europe could spread to and destabilise Belarus, and repeated his offer to host peace talks.

belarus|2026-10-31|gomel|humanitarian.text: 31 Oct — Gomel: Four evacuation flights carrying hundreds of residents from occupied Oleshky (Kherson Oblast) landed in Gomel, from where evacuees continued to Ukrainian-controlled territory, making Belarus a transit point for the US-brokered humanitarian arrangement.

belarus|2026-11-11|minsk|diplomatic.text: 11 Nov — Minsk: In a message for Poland's Independence Day, Lukashenka said Minsk is ready to resume dialogue with Warsaw and urged both sides to drop confrontation (per UA.News; not yet confirmed by other outlets).

moldova|2026-11-11|southern border from.text: 11 Nov — Southern border (from Odesa Oblast): Two Russian Banderol (S8000) cruise missiles entered Moldovan airspace at 06:04 and 06:06 during an overnight attack on Ukraine and left after four to five minutes, per the Defence Ministry. No impacts or casualties were reported.

moldova|2026-10-31|ri bnit a ca la ras i.text: 31 Oct — Rîbnița/Călărași and Dondușeni/Edineț districts: Two Russian drones violated Moldovan airspace during mass attacks on Ukraine, one routed over the Transnistrian region; the Defence Ministry temporarily closed airspace over the north and centre. No crashes or casualties were reported.

georgia|2026-11-09|tbilisi|political.text: 9 Nov — Tbilisi: The Constitutional Court postponed the scheduled resumption of the Georgian Dream petition to ban five opposition parties because a judge fell ill. Hearings resume on 12 November with judges questioning party representatives, a stage expected to run to 17 November.

georgia|2026-11-10|geneva|diplomatic.text: 10–11 Nov — Geneva: The 68th round of the Geneva International Discussions on the Abkhazia and South Ossetia conflicts was scheduled, with Russia again pressing for a non-use-of-force agreement; no outcome had been reported at the time of writing.

georgia|2026-11-04|tbilisi|political.text: 4 Nov — Tbilisi: UNM politician Giorgi Baramidze was remanded in custody on a treason (sabotage) charge over remarks about the 1992–93 Abkhazia conflict.

armenia|2026-11-04|yerevan|political.text: 4–5 Nov — Yerevan: Investigators detained Strong Armenia leader Samvel Karapetyan over alleged abuses said to have cost the national power distributor $179mn, and the Anti-Corruption Court ordered him held for one month. His party calls it persecution linked to the constitutional-referendum fight.

armenia|2026-11-10|yerevan nubarashen pr.text: 10 Nov — Yerevan (Nubarashen prison): Opposition-aligned detainee Arsen Gevorgyan died in custody less than three weeks after his arrest; Justice Minister Galyan cited cardiac arrest without giving the underlying cause.

armenia|2026-11-11|yerevan|unrest.text: 11 Nov — Yerevan: Strong Armenia protested outside the EU Delegation over what it calls political persecution and EU silence; Moscow has condemned Yerevan's pressure on the opposition.

azerbaijan|2026-11-08|baku|political.text: 8 Nov — Baku: Azerbaijan marked Victory Day, the sixth anniversary of the 2020 war, with official ceremonies and a concert on Baku Boulevard; no security incidents were reported.

azerbaijan|2026-11-02|goytepe iranian bo.text: 2–3 Nov — Goytepe (Iranian border): Border guards shot dead an armed man who opened fire while crossing illegally from Iran; a criminal case was opened and Tehran was notified. Drones that entered Azerbaijani airspace were neutralised and drug-smuggling attempts in the Horadiz and Goytepe areas were stopped.

azerbaijan|2026-11-04|baku|diplomatic.text: 4 Nov — Baku: Azerbaijan declared 14 Iranian citizens persona non grata over statements it called hostile. The closed preliminary hearing against Popular Front chairman Ali Karimli, charged with attempting to seize power, began, with the trial on the merits set for 13 November.

mali|2026-11-02|se vare konna road mopti.text: 2 Nov — Sévaré–Konna road, Mopti region: JNIM claimed an IED strike on a vehicle carrying Malian soldiers and Russian Africa Corps personnel. Casualties and location rest only on the group's claim; Bamako released no toll.

mali|2026-11-06|about 50 km south west o.text: 6 Nov — About 50 km south-west of Ménaka: The army general staff said it struck a group of armed fighters with war materiel after confirming the target. It gave no casualty figures.

mali|2026-11-07|about 90 km south of kid.text: 7 Nov — About 90 km south of Kidal: The army said it struck six positions held by armed groups and that reconnaissance was continuing to assess the results. No toll was given.

niger|2026-11-05|niamey|diplomatic.text: 5 Nov — Niamey: Mali's leader Assimi Goïta visited Niamey, where he and Gen. Tiani praised the unified AES force's results against terrorism, according to Nigerien media.

niger|ongoing|niamey|diplomatic.text: c. 10–12 Nov — Niamey: The junta again protested against what it called the EU's 'repeated interference' in its internal affairs. Following protests from Niamey and Algiers, an EU spokesperson issued a clarification.

burkina faso|2026-11-06|nationwide|other.text: 6 Nov — Nationwide: AFP analysis reported that large-scale jihadist attacks have stopped since late June, but that attacks remain frequent and less deadly. Analysts attribute the lull to operational factors rather than any loss of jihadist capability.

burkina faso|ongoing|burkina faso|ground.text: Late Oct — Burkina Faso: The state news agency AIB reported that the army killed a JNIM commander accused of several attacks on the army and VDP militias.

sudan|2026-11-10|bani shako kurmuk count.place: Bani Shako, Kurmuk county, Blue Nile
sudan|2026-11-10|bani shako kurmuk count.text: 10 Nov — Bani Shako, Kurmuk county, Blue Nile: An RSF drone strike killed nine civilians and seriously injured several others, according to the Kurmuk commissioner. The RSF did not comment.

sudan|2026-11-06|maqja bau locality blue.text: 6 Nov — Maqja, Bau locality, Blue Nile: The RSF–SPLM-N 'Tasis' alliance released videos of its fighters inside Maqja, about 90 km from Ed Damazin. The army neither confirmed nor denied the loss; the regional government acknowledged changes in territorial control.

sudan|2026-11-05|north west kordofan|gro.text: 5–6 Nov — North/West Kordofan: The army and the Joint Force launched simultaneous attacks on RSF positions. The Joint Force claimed to have retaken Umm Sumayma, Kazgeil, Al-Hammadi and Abu Quoud and destroyed 40 vehicles, while pro-RSF media claimed an ambush and an army retreat to El Obeid. Neither claim was verified.

sudan|2026-11-04|assosa gedaref|diplomat.text: 4 Nov — Assosa/Gedaref: Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese consular staff and closed Sudan's consulate in Assosa, and Sudan closed Ethiopia's consulate in Gedaref in response. Khartoum accuses Ethiopia of allowing drone attacks from its territory, which Addis Ababa denies.

chad|2026-10-30|koula hadjer lamis bahr.text: 30 Oct — Koula (Hadjer-Lamis/Bahr El-Ghazal border): A dispute over access to a pond between a Kreda herder and a Kouka farmer escalated into armed intercommunal clashes. The territorial administration ministry confirmed 25 dead and 22 wounded, and 39 people were arrested and transferred to N'Djamena.

chad|2026-11-11|abe che ouaddai|politica.text: 11 Nov — Abéché, Ouaddaï: President Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno held the fourth stage of a security tour of the east, focusing on local security and relations between communities.

chad|ongoing|tibesti|ground-clash.text: 5–12 Nov — Tibesti: No new official information on the army's fighting with the Miski Self-Defence Committee, which began on 14 Oct. The lack of news is not evidence that the clashes have ended.

nigeria|2026-11-07|gidan taba maradun lg.text: 7 Nov — Gidan Taba, Maradun LGA, Zamfara: Gunmen killed a vigilante and ten members of his family and set their house on fire, according to police, who also reported 13 residents abducted. Some reports put the toll at 12.

nigeria|2026-11-08|bel village barkin la.place: Bel village, Barkin Ladi LGA, Plateau
nigeria|2026-11-08|bel village barkin la.text: 8 Nov — Bel village, Barkin Ladi LGA, Plateau: Gunmen killed three civilians and a soldier, part of attacks in Plateau and Benue that killed at least 11 people over 3–8 Nov.

nigeria|2026-11-10|near wulgo momaduru n.text: 10 Nov — Near Wulgo–Momaduru, Ngala LGA, Borno: Operation Hadin Kai air strikes hit a large gathering of suspected fighters; the military said 40 ISWAP fighters were killed. The toll is not independently verified.

nigeria|ongoing|bulabulutube borno and g.text: c. 10–11 Nov — Bulabulutube (Borno) and Gujba (Yobe): The military said air strikes and a joint ground ambush killed at least 20 suspected terrorists, including ISWAP fighters. The claim is not independently verified.

north korea|2026-11-02|undisclosed site|.text: 2 Nov — Undisclosed site (KCNA, 3 Nov): North Korea tested a dispersal (cluster) warhead for a strategic cruise missile, the second new cluster-type warhead trial in a week.

north korea|2026-11-04|sondok south hamg.text: 4 Nov — Sondok, South Hamgyong: Multiple missiles were fired toward the East Sea, which Reuters called the fourth weapons launch in a month. The same day KCNA said a newly designed advanced air-defence missile system was test-fired, guided by CMC member Gen. Kim Jong Sik, alongside a strategic cruise-missile strike drill.

north korea|2026-11-04|pyongyang|cyber.text: 3–4 Nov — Pyongyang: Kim Yo Jong called US allegations that North Korea stole more than $6 billion from Binance 'absurd' and warned of a stronger response to US 'hostile policy'. On 6 Nov the US cut off the exchanger MEXC over transactions involving North Korea.

north korea|2026-11-10|pyongyang|politic.text: 10 Nov — Pyongyang: Kim Yo Jong rejected UN Secretary-General Guterres' call for inter-Korean dialogue, accused him of speaking for Seoul, and again denied responsibility for the September DMZ mine blast.

myanmar|2026-11-07|nyaung pin le village.place: Nyaung Pin Le village, Kani Township, Sagaing
myanmar|2026-11-07|nyaung pin le village.text: 7 Nov — Nyaung Pin Le village, Kani Township, Sagaing: Three regime gyrocopters dropped bombs on a school and homes at about 11:30, killing 11 people, including teachers and children, and injuring about 10, according to m.CDM and Myanmar Now.

myanmar|2026-11-06|mazaw village ler mu.place: Mazaw village, Ler Mu Lah Township
myanmar|2026-11-06|mazaw village ler mu.text: 6 Nov — Mazaw village, Ler Mu Lah Township (KNU Myeik-Dawei District): The KNU said an airstrike by a fighter jet and three gyrocopters killed three civilians, including a child, and injured seven, damaging a preschool building.

myanmar|ongoing|kyaikto township mon sta.place: Kyaikto Township, Mon State, and Salingyi Township, Sagaing
myanmar|ongoing|kyaikto township mon sta.text: 3–6 Nov — Kyaikto Township, Mon State, and Salingyi Township, Sagaing: Junta ground operations forced resistance forces to withdraw from a base near Khamauk Khwe and displaced more than 15,000 residents. On 6 Nov troops burned hundreds of houses in Kyaing Khamauk village, Salingyi.

myanmar|2026-11-11|nationwide|ground-cla.text: 11 Nov — Nationwide: The junta said its forces had taken eleven positions from the NUG, KNU and PDFs since early November, including an NUG 'Special Military Region'. The claim has not been independently verified.

pakistan|2026-11-11|darbukach gumbat are.place: Darbukach, Gumbat area near Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
pakistan|2026-11-11|darbukach gumbat are.text: 11 Nov — Darbukach, Gumbat area near Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Militants ambushed a police team returning from an operation against illegal gold mining, killing 10 police including DSP Haidar Zaman and wounding 12. Police said 18 attackers were killed, and the TTP claimed responsibility as part of a series of attacks.

pakistan|2026-11-07|janta sararogha tehs.place: Janta, Sararogha tehsil, Upper South Waziristan
pakistan|2026-11-07|janta sararogha tehs.text: 7 Nov — Janta, Sararogha tehsil, Upper South Waziristan: An IED killed Abdul Jabbar, an assistant head of the police Bomb Disposal Squad, as he tried to defuse it.

pakistan|2026-11-05|shalozan sector kurr.text: 5 Nov — Shalozan sector, Kurram: Pakistani troops exchanged heavy-weapons fire with Afghan Taliban forces after stopping an attempted cross-border infiltration by suspected TTP militants. Casualties were not established and ISPR did not comment.

pakistan|ongoing|mohmand district kp|arm.text: Early Nov — Mohmand district, KP: Unidentified gunmen killed two policemen and wounded one, Dawn reported.

india|2026-11-12|taphou village senapati.text: 12 Nov — Taphou village, Senapati district, Manipur: Gunmen fired on villagers working in paddy fields along NH-2, killing a woman and wounding two men. Organiser blames suspected Kuki militants, which is unverified. The CM had visited Taphou on 9 Nov to defuse tensions after two local youths were found dead on 1 Nov.

india|2026-11-12|sinakeithel village ukh.text: 12 Nov — Sinakeithel village, Ukhrul district, Manipur: Suspected armed miscreants fired from the Lungter Hills at farmers harvesting paddy and wounded one. Security forces returned fire.

india|2026-11-11|kulgam jammu and kashmi.text: 11 Nov — Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir: Unidentified gunmen opened fire on a CRPF patrol, injuring three personnel, one critically. A search for two militants resumed.

india|2026-11-12|kishtwar jammu and kash.text: 11–12 Nov — Kishtwar, Jammu and Kashmir: The bodies of two missing Special Police Officers were found with bullet wounds and their service weapons missing, and police suspect militants.

china|ongoing|western pacific around tai.text: 3–10 Nov — Western Pacific / around Taiwan: Taiwan's NSC said on 3 Nov that more than 100 PLAN and CCG ships were operating off Taiwan, in the South China Sea and in the Pacific. AEI/ISW link task groups from the Eastern, Northern and Southern Theater Commands, including the Liaoning carrier group, to an unannounced exercise simulating Taiwan's isolation. On 10 Nov Taiwan's defence minister called it 'area denial' drills, while Beijing has declared no exercise.

china|2026-11-02|sanya hainan|military-a.text: 2 Nov — Sanya, Hainan: According to AEI/ISW, satellite imagery showed the carrier Fujian leaving Sanya and heading east, after at least three other major surface combatants had sortied between 26 Oct and 2 Nov.

china|2026-11-09|senkaku islands|maritim.text: 9 Nov — Senkaku Islands: Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters near Kuba Island for about two hours, the first such entry since 10 Oct (Jiji).

china|ongoing|kinmen|maritime.text: 2, 4 and 6 Nov — Kinmen: Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration recorded CCG ships in Kinmen's restricted waters on three days in one week.

taiwan|ongoing|around taiwan|military-ac.text: 2–8 Nov — Around Taiwan: The MND recorded 111 PLA aircraft sorties (78 entering the ADIZ), 53 PLAN vessel detections and 36 official ships, all up week on week, per Taiwan Security Monitor. There were median-line crossings on 2, 4 and 6 Nov and 'joint air-sea training' on 4 Nov.

taiwan|2026-11-10|taipei|military-activi.text: 10 Nov — Taipei: Defence Minister Wellington Koo confirmed China is conducting 'area denial' drills in the Western Pacific with the Liaoning carrier group, after the NSC reported more than 100 Chinese naval and coast guard ships around Taiwan and in the Pacific.

taiwan|ongoing|kinmen and pratas|maritim.text: 2–7 Nov — Kinmen and Pratas: The CGA recorded CCG ships in Kinmen restricted waters on 2, 4 and 6 Nov, and a CCG vessel operated near the Pratas Islands on 7 Nov. On 3 Nov the research vessel Haiyang Dizhi 8 and four Chinese fishing boats were spotted near Kaohsiung port.

taiwan|2026-11-06|taipei|other.text: 6–7 Nov — Taipei: The TAIEX fell 1,873 points on 6 Nov amid the PLA surge, and the government activated its NT$500 billion National Stabilization Fund on 7 Nov.

philippines|2026-11-03|scarborough bajo.text: 3 Nov — Scarborough (Bajo de Masinloc) Shoal: The PCG said it was still assessing a Chinese vessel carrying unidentified sensor-fitted equipment inside the lagoon, whose bow and IMO numbers match no known research ship. The CCG announced 'law-enforcement patrols' at the shoal the same day.

philippines|2026-11-08|mamasapano maguin.text: 8 Nov — Mamasapano, Maguindanao del Sur: Unidentified gunmen ambushed and killed three people, including two CAFGU active auxiliaries (Philstar).

philippines|2026-11-08|mindanao|armed-at.text: 8 Nov — Mindanao: Three soldiers were wounded in crossfire while trying to stop a clash between the Labao and Gaosil Maranao clans (Philstar).

philippines|2026-11-04|subic bay|militar.text: 4 Nov — Subic Bay: The US delivered T38 Devil Ray unmanned surface vessels to the Philippine Marines amid continued Chinese pressure in the South China Sea.

south korea|2026-11-04|east sea|missile-.text: 4 Nov — East Sea: The JCS detected multiple North Korean missiles launched from Sondok, South Hamgyong, the North's fourth weapons launch in a month and its 11th suspected ballistic launch of 2026, ahead of combined ROK–US drills.

south korea|ongoing|inter korean border|.text: 1–2 Nov — Inter-Korean border: The ROK military said it had not confirmed any operation of North Korean loudspeakers aimed at the South despite Kim Yo Jong's October deadline. North Korean MDL crossings during fortification work continue to draw warning broadcasts and warning shots, mostly on the eastern front.

south korea|2026-11-10|seoul dmz|politic.text: 10 Nov — Seoul / DMZ: Kim Yo Jong rejected the UN Secretary-General's call for dialogue and called Seoul's findings on the 21 Sep DMZ mine blast, which wounded three ROK officers, fabricated. A joint ROK–UNC investigation attributed the blast to North Korean mines.

vietnam|2026-11-09|hanoi|diplomatic.text: 9 Nov — Hanoi: Vietnam and Australia held their defence policy dialogue, part of Hanoi's continued defence hedging after Indian NSA Ajit Doval's 2 Nov visit agreed co-production and maritime information-sharing.

vietnam|ongoing|ban keun laos|military-a.text: Early Nov — Ban Keun, Laos (Vietnam's western flank): A Vietnamese official told AP that a Chinese deployment to the new Ban Keun airfield in Laos would 'naturally place a certain degree of additional military pressure on Vietnam'.

vietnam|ongoing|vietnam china border|dip.text: 10–11 Nov — Vietnam–China border: Hanoi and Beijing agreed to strengthen coordination on border management and protection. No Vietnam–China maritime incident was found for 5–12 Nov.

japan|2026-11-09|senkaku islands near ku.text: 9 Nov — Senkaku Islands (near Kuba Island): Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters and left about two hours later, the first such entry since 10 Oct (Jiji via Nippon.com).

japan|2026-11-01|miyako strait|military-.text: 1 Nov — Miyako Strait: According to the Joint Staff, a Chinese destroyer and a fast combat support ship transited into the Pacific, and the destroyer later returned to the East China Sea.

japan|2026-11-02|okinawa miyako gap|mili.text: 2 Nov — Okinawa–Miyako gap: The ASDF scrambled fighters against Chinese WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance drones flying from the East China Sea into the Pacific and back.

japan|ongoing|western pacific|military-a.text: 3–10 Nov — Western Pacific: More than 100 Chinese naval and coast guard ships, including the Liaoning carrier group, were deployed in clusters between Taiwan and Guam, which Taiwan calls 'area denial' drills against outside intervention.

indonesia|2026-11-08|camp biru dekai dis.text: 8 Nov — Camp Biru, Kali Senami, Dekai District, Yahukimo, Highland Papua: TNI troops (Satgas Rajawali V and Marines) fought a TPNPB-OPM group led by Kopitua Heluka, pushed back about 15 fighters and took their camp, seizing seven firearms. No casualties were reported.

indonesia|2026-11-08|papua|other.text: 8 Nov (report) — Papua: The Operation Damai Cartenz 2026 task force said it had arrested a suspect in the shooting death of police officer Brigpol Ronald Enok and seized seven firearms from armed groups (Metro TV).

indonesia|2026-10-29|maybrat southwest p.text: 29 Oct — Maybrat, Southwest Papua: Marines detained three alleged TPNPB-OPM members whom the military links to attacks on security posts and Trans-Bintuni road workers.

thailand|2026-11-09|ban kampong baru mae.place: Ban Kampong Baru, Mae Wat, Than To district, Yala
thailand|2026-11-09|ban kampong baru mae.text: 9 Nov — Ban Kampong Baru, Mae Wat, Than To district, Yala: Security forces killed alleged insurgent trainer Sa-udi Ting-useng, wanted over the 2019 Lam Phaya attack that killed 15, in a dawn gunfight about 1 km from the Malaysian border during a three-day operation. Other suspects escaped.

thailand|2026-11-07|maha wan subdistrict.place: Maha Wan subdistrict, Mae Sot, Tak
thailand|2026-11-07|maha wan subdistrict.text: 7 Nov — Maha Wan subdistrict, Mae Sot, Tak: Artillery shells from fighting between Myanmar junta troops and resistance forces in Myawaddy Township landed in Thailand, damaging several houses without injuries.

bangladesh|2026-11-03|joydebpur gazipur|.text: 3 Nov — Joydebpur, Gazipur: Garment worker Toufiq Hossain died of injuries sustained in a clash during the minimum-wage protests, HRW said, the first confirmed death of the unrest. HRW reported police using batons and tear gas against thousands of workers.

bangladesh|2026-11-12|mouchak kaliakair.text: 12 Nov — Mouchak, Kaliakair, Gazipur: Workers blocked the Dhaka–Tangail highway for about three hours. Police fired sound grenades to clear it, and seven factories in the area declared a holiday (Prothom Alo).

bangladesh|ongoing|gazipur|unrest.text: Early Nov — Gazipur: Two garment factories were shut indefinitely after workers vandalised their premises, as protests for a Tk 30,000 minimum wage continued across Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur and Narayanganj.

sri lanka|2026-11-02|kappalthurai uppuve.text: 2 Nov — Kappalthurai, Uppuveli, Trincomalee: A gunman with a suspected T-56 rifle fired on a hired three-wheeler, killing one man (identified by police as a Navy serviceman) and wounding two. Police suspect a drug-trafficking dispute.

sri lanka|2026-11-06|dikwella matara|oth.text: 6 Nov — Dikwella, Matara: Police arrested the suspected gunman in the Trincomalee shooting, a former army soldier who had been formally discharged.

venezuela|2026-10-30|apure state|airstri.text: 30 Oct (reported 5–10 Nov) — Apure state: Venezuelan armed forces struck an ELN camp and cocaine site near the Colombian border, with US drones and intelligence according to The New York Times and with Colombian-supplied coordinates according to Cambio. Reported deaths range from about nine (La Silla Vacia) to 23 (FundaRedes); Caracas has not commented publicly.

venezuela|2026-11-06|el rodeo i prison m.text: 6 Nov — El Rodeo I prison, Miranda: Maria Corina Machado visited relatives of political prisoners camped outside the prison and demanded the release of all of them. Foro Penal counts 322 political prisoners still held.

venezuela|2026-11-08|caracas|political.text: 8 Nov — Caracas: Opposition negotiator Dinorah Figuera said the government will soon release a new group of political prisoners ahead of a fourth round of talks. The families dismantled the protest camp at El Rodeo I after about 10 months, and US Secretary of State Rubio urged foreign minister Oliver Blanco to continue the releases.

colombia|2026-11-07|santa rosa del sur b.text: 7 Nov — Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolivar: Explosive drones struck an army post, killing three soldiers and wounding at least 16, according to the military. Local reports put the toll higher. The ELN and the Clan del Golfo operate in the area; no group has been formally named.

colombia|2026-11-09|tibu norte de santan.text: 9 Nov — Tibu, Norte de Santander (Catatumbo): The government's seventh bombing ('Operation Noah') hit a camp of FARC dissident Front 33. Four alleged members were killed and six captured, including a commission leader close to 'Andrey Avendano', with US MQ-9 surveillance support.

colombia|2026-11-10|undisclosed location.text: 10 Nov — Undisclosed location: President De la Espriella announced an eighth air strike, at 22:17, against an unnamed 'narcoterrorist structure'. No location or casualties have been released yet.

colombia|ongoing|choco|ground-clash.text: 9 Nov — Choco: Fighting between the Clan del Golfo and the ELN has displaced Indigenous families as far as Medellin, with reports of kidnappings and killings.

haiti|2026-11-06|cite soleil port au pri.text: 5–6 Nov — Cite Soleil, Port-au-Prince: Boston gang leader Mathias Saintil (Viv Ansanm) was killed in a security operation that a rights group says used explosive drones. PM Fils-Aime confirmed his death. The rights group reported five gang members killed and about 15 injured in that strike.

haiti|2026-11-05|port au prince|diplomat.text: 5 Nov — Port-au-Prince: The US Embassy in San Salvador formally protested what it called poor Salvadoran coordination, alleging Salvadoran gunfire struck the US Embassy compound in Haiti and nearly hit US personnel. El Salvador rejected the claim on 9 November.

haiti|2026-11-08|near port au prince|dro.actor: Haitian police drone task force / Salvadoran forces
haiti|2026-11-08|near port au prince|dro.text: 8 Nov — Near Port-au-Prince: An early-morning strike by the police drone task force, backed by contractors and Salvadoran helicopters, destroyed a house used by 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph. He was not inside. Reports of up to 20 gunmen killed are unconfirmed, and rights groups and the UN have raised concerns about civilian harm.

haiti|ongoing|haiti|political.text: 8–10 Nov — Haiti: Wilson Joseph proposed 18 November as the start of negotiations. Rubio said El Salvador is operating separately from the international force, and the four Salvadoran technicians kidnapped on 18 October remain missing.

cuba|2026-11-07|el cobre santiago de cub.text: 7 Nov — Guamuta/El Cobre, Santiago de Cuba: Special forces and State Security raided the home of Yoel Alejandro Perez Serrano, who runs a free-meals project for more than 400 people, and detained him. Dozens of residents, including mothers with small children, marched through El Cobre demanding his release. His wife and some protesters were reportedly detained.

cuba|2026-11-08|el cobre|political.text: 8–9 Nov — El Cobre: Food trucks appeared in El Cobre and Guamuta the day after the protest. As of 9 November, Perez Serrano had not been released and authorities had not disclosed where he is held or any charges.

cuba|2026-11-04|nationwide|humanitarian.text: 4 Nov — Nationwide: The Electric Union forecast 960 MW available against peak demand of 2,850 MW, a generation deficit of about 1,890 MW with seven thermal units out of service.

ecuador|2026-11-08|manabi|armed-attack.text: 7–8 Nov — Manabi: Primicias reported 19 killings in three days across Montecristi, Manta, Bolivar, Portoviejo, Sucre, El Carmen, Pedernales and Jipijapa, including three people shot dead in Calceta on 7 November and two men killed in a house in Montecristi on 8 November. Manabi has recorded 1,018 violent deaths in 2026.

ecuador|2026-11-08|calceta manabi|armed-.text: 8 Nov — Calceta, Manabi: Local news-page journalist Tomas Beltran was shot dead outside his home. He had reported death threats and was in the prosecutor's witness-protection system; the Inter American Press Association condemned the killing.

ecuador|2026-11-09|guayaquil|armed-attac.text: 9 Nov — Guayaquil (via a la Costa km 22): Gunmen attacked a pickup truck at the entrance to a residential development, killing two women.

ecuador|2026-11-10|guayas manabi los rio.place: Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro, Esmeraldas
ecuador|2026-11-10|guayas manabi los rio.text: 8–10 Nov — Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro, Esmeraldas: The Interior Ministry reported 2,292 people captured in the curfew's first week, with 204 firearms and 612 kg of drugs seized. The fourth curfew of 2026 ended at 05:00 on 10 November, ahead of the 29 November local elections.

peru|ongoing|lima callao|armed-attack.text: Week to 7 Nov — Lima/Callao: America TV counted six extortion attacks on public transport and three deaths in a week, in districts including San Juan de Lurigancho, Callao, Villa El Salvador, Surquillo, Carabayllo and Chorrillos, including bus driver Josue Perdomo Estrada, shot six times in Chorrillos. The Public Ministry recorded 169 extortion attacks on transport companies (95 dead) between January and October 2026.

peru|2026-11-10|lima|unrest.text: 10 Nov — Lima: More than 50 public transport companies suspended service for a march from Plaza de Acho to Congress against extortion and driver killings, threatening a strike if the government does not act. Heavy-cargo hauliers separately announced a 72-hour national strike for 16–18 November over diesel prices.

peru|2026-11-11|lima callao|other.text: 11 Nov — Lima/Callao: Pope Leo XIV's visit began under a security plan of more than 37,000 police nationwide (22,464 in Lima and Callao) and drone-flight restrictions in six cities through 16 November.

bolivia|2026-11-06|patacamaya|military-a.text: 6–7 Nov — Patacamaya/La Paz: Police deployed 450 officers to control Patacamaya and eight entry points to La Paz ahead of the Morales-aligned march called for 6 November. Police reported no irregularities and normal traffic, and no blockades or clashes were reported.

bolivia|2026-11-11|la paz|political.text: 11 Nov — La Paz: Government Minister Marco Antonio Oviedo called Evo Morales 'the chief of a cartel' trafficking drugs from the Chapare (Tropico de Cochabamba). He said police detected more than 8 million bolivianos moving from the Tropico to finance the May–June blockades, which left 16 dead.

bolivia|2026-11-12|la paz|political.text: 12 Nov — La Paz: Defence Minister Ernesto Justiniano said the armed forces are being prepared to confront 'narcoterrorism' in support of, not in place of, the police, citing lessons from the 53-day crisis.

dominican republic|2026-11-10|santo domi.text: 10 Nov — Santo Domingo: President Abinader confirmed that the Dominican Republic provides logistics and intelligence to Salvadoran forces fighting gangs in Haiti and urged better coordination between them and the GSF. He said the southern border has been reinforced and gang activity remains concentrated in and around Port-au-Prince.

dominican republic|2026-11-04|dajabon el.text: 4 Nov — Dajabon, Elias Pina, Jimani, Pedernales: The Defence Minister toured four crossings and called the border 'totally calm'. About 11,000 troops are deployed along the frontier, and the government says it could close the border if needed.

jamaica|2026-11-08|st elizabeth|armed-at.text: 8 Nov — St Elizabeth (Monymusk and Williamsfield areas): In predawn operations, security forces fatally shot two murder suspects, Dadrian White and Oshane Wright, in two separate 'alleged confrontations' about 45 minutes apart. Police say two firearms were recovered.

jamaica|2026-11-04|st elizabeth|armed-at.text: 4 Nov — St Elizabeth: A man was fatally shot by a licensed firearm holder at a bar.

jamaica|2026-11-03|manchester|armed-atta.text: 3 Nov — Manchester: Police said a man killed in a firefight with officers was on his way to carry out a contract killing, the third police killing in Manchester and St Catherine in about a week.
